pr_title: Fix multiple harvester dock sequence bugs
pr_body:
Fixes
- drag activity running even if refinery died while turning to dock angle
- dock anim running even if refinery died while dragging towards it
- undock anim playing even if dock anim didn't run for the above or some other reason
- and some more (see commit messages)

Fixes #18422.
Fixes #18733.
pr_comments: > Activities/HarvesterDockSequence.cs(73,1): error SA1028: Code should not contain trailing whitespace [/home/travis/build/OpenRA/OpenRA/OpenRA.Mods.Common/OpenRA.Mods.Common.csproj]

My initial thought was that the code looks sensible, but when I test this by adding `Refinery.Kill(self);` in the `DockingState.Turn` case I find that this doesn't seem to work!

Are you able to reproduce this using the same testcase?

> My initial thought was that the code looks sensible, but when I test this by adding Refinery.Kill(self); in the DockingState.Turn case I find that this doesn't seem to work!
> Are you able to reproduce this using the same testcase?

The code wasn't wrong, it's just that the issue basically consists of multiple bugs.

The problem was that the undock anim would still play on "undock" even if the dock anim hadn't. Fixed that, but I pushed before seeing the above additional suggestions so I'll update this again.

I can still trigger a glitch by issuing a move order while the TD harvester is turning. I thought that adding `IsCancelling` to the check at the start of `DockingState.Drag` would have solved this, but seems not.

> I can still trigger a glitch by issuing a move order while the TD harvester is turning. I thought that adding IsCancelling to the check at the start of DockingState.Drag would have solved this, but seems not.

Updated, should be fixed now (last commit).

Confirmed that this does not fix #18733. Repro case: add `Refinery.Kill(self);` to the start of `case DockingState.Undock:`.

Do you want to fix that here too?
Code changes look good to me and i've confirmed that all the other death cases work correctly.

Updated.

> Do you want to fix that here too?

Should be fixed now, if my eyes didn't deceive me in my quick test.

> Dead actors are never in the world, so I'm not sure if it makes sense here to check both. (Just `IsInWorld` should be enough.)

`IsDead` returns `true` as soon as health drops to zero, while `Actor.Dispose()` only sets `IsInWorld` to `false` in a frame end task. I'm a bit wary of not checking `IsDead`, though admittedly I might be a bit too paranoid here.

There are a bunch of places across the code that check both IsDead and IsInWorld. How about we keep it here and, if/when we're confident that just IsInWorld is the correct change, have a new PR that fixes this everywhere?
Do we have a plan on how to proceed here?

> Do we have a plan on how to proceed here?

While implementing
> We should probably just drop that and add IsCanceling checks where necessary.

I stumbled over another design flaw of the dock sequence, namely that `DockingState.Complete` still unconditionally called `Undocked` on the refinery if it's alive, as well as drag. Since I was recently swamped with work and stuff, I didn't have the mental bandwidth to finish this, but I'm working on it right now and will update soon.
That's quite a different bug (and IMO a rare enough edge case that it may not be worth fixing at all) to the issues being fixed here. Can we track and fix that in a separate issue/PR?
Fair enough, I thought we wanted to tackle all of the while we're here. Done at #18835.
